subtopics.title: Review of Demand and Supply Curves

questions.question: According to the Law of Demand, what happens to the quantity demanded when the price of a good increases, ceteris paribus?
options: The demand curve shifts to the right

questions.question: Which of the following describes the shape of a typical supply curve?
What does the phrase 'ceteris paribus' mean in economics?
Market equilibrium occurs when:
options: Quantity demanded exactly equals quantity supplied
Quantity demanded is greater than quantity supplied
Quantity supplied is greater than quantity demanded

questions.question: If the current market price is set above the equilibrium price, what is the result?
How do market forces react to a shortage?
Beef is considered a normal good. What happens to the demand curve for beef if consumer income increases?
options: There is a movement upward along the curve
There is a movement downward along the curve

questions.question: When the demand curve shifts to the right and the supply curve remains unchanged, what happens to the equilibrium price?
When the demand curve shifts to the right and the supply curve remains unchanged, what happens to the equilibrium quantity?
Why does the supply curve not shift when consumer income increases?
options: Consumer income is a non-price determinant of demand, not supply
Supply only shifts when price changes
It does shift, but we ignore it

questions.question: Which of the following causes a shift of the demand curve rather than a movement along it?
options: A change in the price of the good itself
A change in the cost of production

questions.question: In a market graph, which axis typically represents Price?
What is the ultimate effect of a rightward shift in demand (ceteris paribus) on market equilibrium?
options: Higher equilibrium price and higher equilibrium quantity
Lower equilibrium price and lower equilibrium quantity
Higher equilibrium price and lower equilibrium quantity
Lower equilibrium price and higher equilibrium quantity
